findings.title: Minimal explore .openspec.yaml contents unspecified — conflicts with the required `schema` field the reused helpers enforce
findings.recommendation: The delta requires explore Mode B/C to write "a minimal `.openspec.yaml` (same metadata genre as changes)" and design.md D2 claims `readChangeMetadata`/`writeChangeMetadata` are reused unchanged — but `writeChangeMetadata` (src/utils/change-metadata.ts) Zod-requires `schema` and calls `validateSchemaName`, which throws on any name not in the schema registry. Nothing in the deltas, design, or task 2.2 says what base fields the minimal explore file carries (which `schema` value? `created`? `schema_version`?). Codegen must guess, and either choice strains a stated claim (a `schema: spec-driven` line in an exploration is semantically odd; relaxing the helpers contradicts "unchanged"). Specify the minimal file's contents explicitly — e.g. `schema: spec-driven` + `created` mirroring change metadata (which also makes the propose merge rule's fresh-fields-win concretely meaningful) — in the orbit-explore-modifications delta, design D2, and task 2.2.

findings.title: Un-delta'd pass-surface enumeration: recommendation_options "When to emit" covers only 9 proposal + 7 system passes
findings.recommendation: The live baseline's `Optional recommendation_options field on finding entries` requirement scopes its normative emit rule to "all 9 proposal-mode passes + 7 system-mode passes" — a full-surface enumeration D2 outgrows by adding six architecture-mode passes whose findings are, per the delta, ingestible by /orbit:address-reviews exactly like other internal review JSON (and the modified `Internal run summary persisted per mode` scenario includes `recommendation_options` for architecture-mode summaries). Same enumeration class that produced prior CRITICALs (final-assessment scoping; Emit timing); here there is no hard contradiction (omission degrades to the prose-recommendation fallback), so WARNING. Add a MODIFIED block extending the "When to emit" scope to the architecture-mode passes.

findings.title: Generated-file disposition's orbit-authored enumeration not extended to orbit-architect
findings.recommendation: The `Generated-file disposition` requirement's orbit-authored scenario enumerates the category's members (currently `orbit-onboard` + the four net-new editorial workflows). `orbit-architect` is a fully orbit-authored 16th template (design D6) but no delta adds it, leaving the disposition list stale the moment architect lands — the exact list audit-drift Category 3 would then flag, and inconsistent with how this change DID delta the analogous orbit-onboard identity enumeration. Add a small orbit-conventions MODIFIED block adding `orbit-architect` to the orbit-authored enumeration (optionally also retiring the now-landed "when they land" future tense, which is pre-existing B3-era wording).

findings.title: D2 state line's cycle counts are stale vs the on-disk trail (5 passes/30 findings vs 6 passes/34 findings)
findings.recommendation: The hand-maintained D2 state line says "across 5 review passes (fresh x3, external x2 — 30 findings, all resolved)" but the change's `.orbit-runs/` shows 4 internal proposal reviews (12+6+6+4 = 28 findings) plus 2 externals (3+3 = 6) — 6 passes, 34 findings — and this iteration-5 run lags it further. Harmless in the long run (the retrofit deletes every state line — the change's own thesis), but until apply this line is the arc's manual position record. Correct the counts on next touch, or replace them with a pointer to the trail rather than hand-copied numbers.

findings.title: Status rendering of a malformed doc's well-formed stages is ambiguous between two scenarios
findings.recommendation: `Citations resolve against a malformed doc's well-formed stages` (line 154) says such stages participate in state computation, while `Status buckets parseable, legacy, and malformed docs` (line 177) says malformed docs are listed with their grammar violations in the `malformed` bucket — whether `status` also renders per-stage computed state for the well-formed stages of a malformed doc (and in which bucket) is unspecified. One sentence in either scenario would settle it for codegen (e.g. "a malformed doc's well-formed stages render their computed state within the malformed listing").
